title: The load, verify, approve and rollback surface of the permission matrix and the delegation of authority table is rwb-case's under the Ownership Map, while the tables and every validation rule that decides a refusal are rwb-access's
source: API Specification v4 x-module P4 for /admin/lists/{listCode} and /admin/reference-loads, /approve, /verify, /rollback; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (permission, delegation_limit), T4 and appendix T-A.1 API-P4-004 to API-P4-010; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 AC-EXC-P4-005-02, A2.5 AC-P4-005-01 and A2.6 AC-P4-006-01; Microservice Ownership Map v1 (plan Appendix R default ruling: parameters and reference data to P3; lov_value to P3; P4 keeps role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit); ASM-A6-tables-4 and ASM-A6-tables-5
section: Section 2.4, section 6 FR-P4-008, FR-P4-009, FR-P4-020, FR-P4-022, section 9, section 10.1, section 12 Q-P4-03
description: Two sources place the reference-load surface in rwb-access and one places it in rwb-case. API Specification v4 and TSD P4 appendix T-A give /admin/reference-loads with approve, verify and rollback and /admin/lists/{listCode} an x-module of P4, and FSD P4 A2.5 and A2.6 build the permission matrix load and the DoA load on those operations, with the loader unable to approve and only the table's approver role allowed to. The Ownership Map rules that parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043) belong to rwb-case (P3) and that P4 keeps only its role, scope, masking and DoA tables. The PRD therefore cannot say who validates a matrix or DoA file, who approves it, who rolls it back and which service exposes the operation, although the validation rules (duplicate role and area row, invalid letters, falling DoA limit, unknown decision code) and the four-eyes rule are P4's business rules. Every Epic 1 policy change path depends on the answer.
evidence: API Specification v4 sets x-module P4 on the eight list and reference-load operations; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-010 with the Reference data right letters; FSD P4 AC-P4-005-01 loads PM-2026.12 with table 'permission' and has RW-SECADM approve it, and AC-P4-006-01 loads DOA-2026.11 with table 'delegation_limit' and has the risk role approve it; the Ownership Map records the reference-data ruling with ASM-A6-api-4 and ASM-A6-tables-5 and rules lov_value to P3 with its reason 'P4 keeps only its role, scope, masking and DoA tables, despite TSD P4 v3 listing lov_value'.
area: rwb-access policy administration, load path and ownership
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case contract owner
proposed: Confirm at the RWB-P3 reference-data contract review that rwb-access publishes the authorise, masking and DoA lookup answers and that the load, approve, verify and rollback operations stay with rwb-case, with the P4 validation rules called as part of that load; if instead the DoA and matrix files are loaded inside rwb-access, restore API-P4-005, 006, 009 and 010 to P4 in the API specification and in appendix T-A and record the ruling on the Ownership Map. Until then this PRD states the load path as a dependency and marks FR-P4-012 and the wave 1 policy administration as load-based through the rwb-case surface.

title: The rule package registry, the rule-package operations and the change report are claimed by the P4 technical specification while the Ownership Map gives them to rwb-decision
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T1, T2 (RulePackageStore, RulePackageAuditService), T3.1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case), T6.3 and appendix T-A.1 API-P4-014 to API-P4-020; FSD P4 A2.18 and FEAT-ADM-02; API Specification v4 x-module P3 for the six rule-package paths; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15; Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling with ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-api-3 (rule package registry to P7)
description: Four rule tables, the rule-package upload, approve, rollback, dry-run and change-report operations and the audit duty are written into the P4 technical specification and one P4 feature (FEAT-ADM-02), but the Ownership Map, Architecture v5 slide 14 (DMN model registry with rwb-decision), slide 27 and the Temporal and Drools design all place rule governance centrally in rwb-decision, with each service holding only a local evaluated copy. The API Specification v4 disagrees with both and marks the six paths x-module P3. The PRD excludes rule administration from every increment and lists it as a dependency, so no P4 requirement or acceptance criterion covers a rule change; the P4 requirements REQ-ACA-013 and the E8 administration feature FEAT-ADM-02 are therefore served outside this service and must be traced to rwb-decision instead.
evidence: TSD P4 T1 reads 'It covers: roles, permissions, scope, masking, delegation of authority table, access log, the rule package store and the workflow administration surface'; T-A.1 lists API-P4-014 to API-P4-020; the Ownership Map ruling reads 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision ... services hold only a local evaluated copy (DP-04), despite TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 declaring these tables'; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-decision the DMN model registry; the API Specification v4 marks the same six paths x-module P3.
area: rwb-access scope, rule package administration and the E8 administration feature set
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-decision contract owner
proposed: Re-issue TSD P4 without the four rule tables, the RulePackageStore and the six rule-package operations, and move FEAT-ADM-02 with its acceptance criteria to the rwb-decision documents; keep in P4 only the rule-evaluation rights that the matrix grants (RULES_AND_PARAMETERS), which FR-P4-010 and FR-P4-013 already cover. Correct the API Specification v4 x-module of the six paths to P7 in the same pass.

title: POST /admin/workflows/smoke is claimed by the P3 and P4 technical specifications while the Ownership Map and Architecture v5 give the smoke workflow to the platform
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T2 (WorkflowAdminService) and API-P4-021; TSD P3 API-P3-027; Architecture v5 slides 44 (JOB-22, rwb-platform) and 20 (every service); Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling with ASM-A6-api-5 (POST /admin/workflows/smoke to PLT)
description: The smoke workflow run is declared as an operation of rwb-access in the P4 technical specification (with 404 when the workflow switch is off) and as an operation of rwb-case in the P3 technical specification, while Architecture v5 slide 44 runs PlatformSmokeWorkflow on task queue rwb-platform under the platform administrator and the Ownership Map rules the path to the platform library. The PRD excludes the operation from P4 and records it as a platform dependency, so the P4 scope carries no workflow administration requirement and the acceptance criteria of FEAT-ADM-01 that concern the smoke run are served outside this service.
evidence: TSD P4 T-A.1 API-P4-021 and T2 WorkflowAdminService; TSD P3 API-P3-027; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-22 'Smoke workflow | 06:00 | platform | Schedule'; Ownership Map ruling: 'Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22 and Batch and Scheduling Design v4 run PlatformSmokeWorkflow on task queue rwb-platform with the platform administrator, so the owner is PLT'.
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform workflow owner
proposed: Remove API-P4-021 and the WorkflowAdminService from TSD P4 and the same path from TSD P3, and keep it once in the platform workflow story and specification, so the E8 administration surface links to the platform capability instead of re-publishing it.

title: lov_value and partner_user are defined in the P4 technical specification but owned by rwb-case and rwb-partner
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (lov_value, DF-REF-027 to 033; partner_user, DF-REF-212 to 217) and T3.3; TSD P4 T3.2 lists; Architecture v5 slide 41 (S9 owns partner users; P3 owns reference data); Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings with ASM-A6-tables-5 and ASM-A6-tables-6
section: Section 2.4, section 3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-SCOPE), section 8 (referenced entities), section 9
description: The P4 technical specification defines a list-of-values table and a partner user table with their columns and a relationship from partner_user to partner. The Ownership Map rules the list of values to rwb-case as reference data and the partner user to rwb-partner, and the PRD therefore treats both as referenced entities owned elsewhere. The consequence is that rwb-access reads the fourteen capability areas, the four scopes, the role classes and the partner identity attributes through another service's contract, and needs an agreed read path and a decision on what it caches; the matrix seed and the session answer both depend on those values.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 'lov_value (NEW). A value in a list of values' with DF-REF-027 to 033 and 'partner_user (NEW). A partner user's identity bound to one partner firm and one partner role' with DF-REF-212 to 217; T3.3 relationship partner_user to partner; Ownership Map: 'lov_value is reference data and stays with P3 ... P4 keeps only its role, scope, masking and DoA tables, despite TSD P4 v3 listing lov_value' and 'Partner users stay with S9 rwb-partner ... P4 keeps the internal role model only, despite TSD P4 v3 defining partner_user'.
area: rwb-access data model and reference reads
proposed: Drop lov_value and partner_user from TSD P4 T3.1 and keep the lists of values in TSD P3 and the partner identity in TSD S9; state in the rwb-access contract which list-of-values versions and which partner identity attributes it reads and how often it refreshes them, so the matrix seed and the session answer are built against one source.

title: The four operations Architecture v5 gives rwb-access first (authorise, /me/permissions, /doa-limits, /masking-policies) have no request or answer schema in the API Specification v4 or the P4 appendix, and the group-to-role mapping has no stated read path
source: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 (IN: POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits · /masking-policies; first API path /authorise); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-021, none of them the authorise path) and T-A.2 (API-P4-012 GET /me/session only); API Specification v4 (no authorise, doa-limits or masking-policies path); FSD P4 A2.1, A2.5, A2.6, A2.14 and A2.30
section: Section 6 FR-P4-006, FR-P4-011, FR-P4-021, FR-P4-016, section 9.1 Q-P4-01 and Q-P4-10, section 12
description: The service contract that every other service depends on is the one with no schema. Architecture v5 names the authorise path as the first API path of rwb-access and lists four input operations, but the API Specification v4 carries none of them and TSD P4 appendix T-A defines only GET /me/session among the session paths. Nothing states what the caller sends (case reference, owner, queue, team, region), what the answer carries (decision, area, right, scope applied, matrix version, masking marker per field, grant marker), how a refusal is distinguished from a not-found, or which attributes of a partner identity travel with the request. Separately, role resolution needs the Entra group and the role row: TSD P4 T3.1 puts entra_group on role, FSD P4 A2.1 names v_ace_iam_group as the ACE read, and no source states the join, the cache or the behaviour when a group maps to a retired role. This PRD has to fix both shapes as a default before the contract review.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 'REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) · GET /me/permissions · GET /doa-limits · /masking-policies' and slide 41 first API path /authorise; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists 18 operations and none is /authorise, /me/permissions, /doa-limits or /masking-policies; T-A.2 defines API-P4-012 GET /me/session with response Session and no field list; the API Specification v4 contains no path for any of the four; FSD P4 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-005-05 names masking version MASK-SIT-01 without listing the fields it covers; TSD P4 T3.1 role carries DF-REF-039 entra_group while FSD P4 A2.1.3.2 calls v_ace_iam_group.entra_group 'not a Workbench column'.
area: rwb-access authorise, masking and DoA contract, and the group-to-role read
proposed: Publish the four operations in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A with their request and answer schemas, the refusal and not-found codes, the version fields and the masking marker vocabulary, and state in TSD P4 T3.1 how a group resolves to a role row and what happens to a session when a role is retired. Then freeze the contract once, so FR-P4-011, FR-P4-021 and the consumer fakes are built against one shape instead of an inferred one.

title: AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged are published by rwb-access in Architecture v5 but have no row, payload, key or refresh window in the event design
source: Architecture v5 slide 14 (EVT rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged) and slide 43 ('AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged | rwb-access | rwb.access.events.v1 | all (cache refresh)'); Event and Messaging Design v4 (no row for either event); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T5.3 ('None'); FSD P4 A2.3, A2.4 and A2.6
section: Section 6 FR-P4-012 and FR-P4-038, section 9, section 9.1 Q-P4-02, section 12
description: Every service is told to refresh its cached authorise answer when the policy changes, and the only mechanism named is an event with no contract. The Event and Messaging Design v4 carries no row for either event, the P4 technical specification states that the module publishes no events (T5.3 'None'), and no source gives the CloudEvents type, the topic (Architecture v5 names rwb.access.events.v1), the partition key, the payload (version label, effective date, change kind), the delivery guarantees or the refresh window a consumer may assume. Without those, FR-P4-012's cache refresh cannot be tested and a policy change may sit unseen in a consumer until it restarts.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access the topic rwb.access.events.v1 with AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged; slide 43 lists both events with consumers 'all (cache refresh)'; the Event and Messaging Design v4 rows checked are EV-08 and its neighbours on the decision-record topic, and neither access event appears; TSD P4 T5.3 records 'None' for events; no source states a payload or a time to live.
area: rwb-access events and consumer cache refresh
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform event owner
proposed: Add both events to the Event and Messaging Design with CloudEvents type, topic, key, payload and versioning, and state the cache refresh window a consumer must honour and the fallback when an event is missed; update TSD P4 T5.3 from 'None' to the two events so the technical specification and Architecture v5 agree.

title: The access log has no stated retention, no stated searchable period, no stated storage object and no stated cross-service read right, although it is the evidence for every access question
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7 (FEAT-ACA-07), A2.8 (FEAT-ACA-08) and A2.16 (FEAT-ACA-16) with AC-P4-009-01 and AC-ALT-P4-009-02; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3 ('decision log linkage') and API-P4-008; Architecture v5 slides 20 (decision_record per service) and 28 (local record, hash-linked); Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-030 and NFR-042; Decision Log v10 DL26
section: Section 6 FR-P4-023 to FR-P4-027, section 8, section 12 Q-P4-04 and Q-P4-14
description: The access log is specified as behaviour but not as data. The FSD says every read and every export is written to the decision log store and searched from the access log, and Architecture v5 gives every service a local decision_record object plus a central ledger in rwb-decision; no source states which object answers the access query, how long an access entry is kept (NFR-030 leaves log retention to Compliance under DL26), how far back the search may go, whether an access entry carries the case's personal data or only identifiers, or which roles outside the service may query it. The access event is also the only evidence for a PDPA question, so the classification and the retention are product decisions, not implementation detail. The PRD fixes the classification as PII and confidential and marks the retention open.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-P4-009-01 writes one decision log entry with decision code AC-READ and the field IDs returned; AC-ALT-P4-009-02 writes AC-EXPT with the filter and the row count; TSD P4 API-P4-008 searches the access log by user, from, to, event, page and size; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service 'Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record'; NFR-030 'The decision log is retained for the period the regulator and internal audit require' with status 'Open, DL26'; NFR-042 'Every read ... is logged' with no period; no source gives an access-log retention, an index, a storage object or a read right for another service.
area: rwb-access access log data, retention and query rights
proposed: Answer DL26 for the access log in one row: the retention period, whether it equals the decision log period, which object answers the query (the local record, the central ledger, or a projection of both), which fields are searchable and for how far back, and which roles in other services may read it. Until then this PRD keeps the classification at PII and marks the retention as not set.

title: The break-glass duration, the minimum reason length and the review window appear only inside acceptance criteria and are open in the decision log
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.9 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 (grant until the earlier of 4 hours and the group end), AC-EXC-P4-009-02 (reason min 20, max 1000) and A2.10; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 API-P4-013; Decision Log v10 DL38 ('Access timers: access review interval, leaver response time and break-glass review window' - not a choice, values from the bank IAM standard, load placeholder values until set); Non-Functional Specification v3 (no break-glass NFR)
section: Section 6 FR-P4-028, FR-P4-029, FR-P4-030, FR-P4-031, section 12 Q-P4-05
description: Two rules that decide whether an emergency action is allowed live only in the acceptance criteria of the functional specification: the grant ends at the earlier of four hours and the end of the IAM group, and the reason must be 20 to 1000 characters. DL38 states that the access timers, including the break-glass review window, are values from the bank IAM standard and are not yet set, and it instructs placeholder values until they are. No parameter table, no list of values and no business rule source carries the numbers, and the review window for a grant is named in the FSD title of FEAT-ACA-10 without a value. The PRD adopts the AC values as a default and records that they are placeholders.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 'the grant is active until 14:30, the earlier of 4 hours and the group end'; AC-EXC-P4-009-02 'message MSG-GEN-002 for field reason with min 20 and max 1000'; DL38 column 'Not a choice. Values from the bank IAM standard.' with the action 'Load placeholder values until set', owner SCB IT security, earliest date 2026-11-06; TSD P4 API-P4-013 defines a BreakGlassActivation request with no field list.
area: rwb-access break-glass parameters and review window
owner_role: SCB IT security with the security administrator
proposed: Answer DL38 with the break-glass maximum duration, the reason bounds, the review window and the review role, and hold them as versioned parameters rather than literals, so FR-P4-028 and FR-P4-031 read them at run time; the four hours and the 20 to 1000 characters stay as the placeholder values until the answer arrives.

title: The six-monthly access review list has no interface, no file layout, no review-date convention and no recipient
source: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44 (JOB-18 Access review list, six-monthly, rwb-access, Schedule); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-18 (produces role holder lists for recertification, owner security administrator); FSD P4 A1.2 (no review feature) and A2.13; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (no extract or staging object); Microservice Ownership Map v1 (JOB-18 to P4)
section: Section 6 FR-P4-033, section 9 (rwb-integration delivery), section 10.3, section 12 Q-P4-05
description: The only scheduled work of the service is a recertification artefact with no shape. Architecture v5 gives the job its name, its cycle, its owner and its mechanism, and the Batch and Scheduling Design says it produces role holder lists, but no source gives the interface row that carries the file, the file pattern, the columns, the review-date convention (cycle start, cycle end or the run date), the recipient or the way a delivery outcome is matched when the file carries no case. The FSD feature list contains no review feature, and the technical specification defines no extract object. The PRD keeps the requirement at capability level and marks the artefact as not specified.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-18 | Access review list | six-monthly | rwb-access | Schedule'; slide 14 'TMP Schedule: access review list (six-monthly)'; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-18 'Produces role holder lists for recertification | Every six months | None | Rerun | Security administrator'; FSD P4 A1.2 lists 30 features and none is the review list; TSD P4 T3.1 defines six P4 tables and no extract; no source names a review interface ID, pattern or recipient.
owner_role: Security administrator with the rwb-integration contract owner
proposed: Register one interface row for the access review file in the versioned interface configuration with its direction, pattern, data product, owner role and alert role, publish the file layout and the review-date convention, and agree with the rwb-integration contract owner how a file-level delivery with no case is matched; then FR-P4-033 becomes testable at file level.

title: The joiner, mover and leaver capability has a Must requirement in Epic 2, a feature code in Epic 1 and no legacy story, and its response times are open under DL38
source: Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.4 (REQ-ACA-011, Must, E2); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A1.2 FEAT-ACA-13 (first in E1) and A2.13; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (role.entra_group) and T6.2; Decision Log v10 DL38 (leaver response time not set) and DL39/DL40 (roles with real users and Entra group names not set); plan split_plan.json (no P4 story for REQ-ACA-011; the nearest is RWB-E2-019 for partner identities)
section: Section 6 FR-P4-032, section 10.2, section 11 AC-P4-028, section 12 Q-P4-05
description: The requirement that access follows the organisation is a Must in Epic 2, its feature is marked first in Epic 1, and the plan carries no story for it: the joiner, mover and leaver path is the only P4 Must requirement without a legacy key, a slice or an acceptance criterion of its own. Its two values, the leaver response time and the access review interval, are open under DL38, and the group names it depends on are open under DL40. The PRD keeps the requirement and states the value as not specified; the backlog has to create the slice before the requirement can be accepted.
evidence: BRD Program v4 section 5.4 'REQ-ACA-011 | Joiner, mover and leaver changes reach the Workbench so that access matches the current organization. | Must | Security administrator | E2'; FSD P4 A1.2 'FEAT-ACA-13 | Apply joiner, mover and leaver changes to access | Admin | ... | E1 | A2.13'; split_plan.json lists for P4 the keys E1-001, E1-007, E1-008, E1-016, E1-018, E1-019, E1-020, E1-021, E1-022, E1-023, E1-028, E1-037 to E1-039, E1-054, E1-062 to E1-065, E1-069, the E2 keys and the AD and E8 keys, and none of them covers the joiner-mover-leaver path; DL38 records the leaver response time as a value from the bank IAM standard, not yet set.
area: rwb-access joiner, mover and leaver access change
owner_role: Business analyst with the security administrator
proposed: Create the Epic 2 story for REQ-ACA-011 in the P4 epic, with the group-change scenario, the session re-resolution, the reallocation hand-off to rwb-case and the leaver response time, and answer DL38 and DL40 so its acceptance criteria can carry a value.

title: No source holds the full role conflict list, the role and permission row counts of a version, or the effective-date column of a matrix version
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 AC-P4-005-01 (matrix PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12, 756 permission rows, validFrom 2026-12-01), AC-EXC-P4-001-03 (RW-SECADM may not hold any business role); legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10 (RW-RISK may not hold RW-REFADM); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (permission has matrix_version and no valid_from; role_conflict has conflict_version, valid_from and valid_to)
section: Section 6 FR-P4-005, FR-P4-008, section 8, section 12 Q-P4-12
description: The role conflict refusal and the effective dating of a matrix version both lack source values. Only two conflict pairs are named anywhere (RW-SECADM with any business role, RW-RISK with RW-REFADM), no source gives the complete list, and the role_conflict version label has no value. The permission table carries matrix_version but no valid-from or valid-to column, while the FSD takes matrix version PM-2026.12 into effect on 2026-12-01 and the acceptance criterion counts 756 permission rows; the target therefore has no named column to date a matrix version. The PRD keeps both behaviours and records the data as not specified, because the seed and the sign-in refusal cannot be built from a partial list.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 'the role conflict table says RW-SECADM may not hold any business role'; legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10 'RW-RISK may not hold RW-REFADM'; TSD P4 T3.1 permission fields DF-REF-040 to 044 with no valid_from and no valid_to, and role_conflict fields DF-REF-205 to 211 with conflict_version, valid_from and valid_to and no value; FSD P4 AC-P4-005-01 'matrix version PM-2026.11' and 'PM-2026.12' with 'validFrom 2026-12-01' and '756 rows'.
area: rwb-access role conflict data and matrix version dating
owner_role: Security administrator with the reference data administrator
proposed: Publish the approved role conflict list with its version label and its effective dates, add the effective-date columns of a matrix version to TSD P4 T3.1 or state that the date lives on the load, and confirm the role and permission row counts of the version in force, so FR-P4-005 and FR-P4-008 can be seeded and tested.

title: The personal field list the masking policy must cover and the content of a masking version are not enumerated in any source
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5 AC-ALT-P4-005-01 (identity number and phone number masked), AC-EXC-P4-005-05 (v_ace_customer.date_of_birth masked as XXXX-XX-XX, masking version MASK-SIT-01), A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 (DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 masked); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 masking_rule (DF-REF-198 to 204); Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-039 and NFR-040; Decision Log v10 DL26
section: Section 6 FR-P4-016, FR-P4-017, FR-P4-018, section 8, section 12 Q-P4-11
description: The masking capability is a Must requirement and its rules are data, but the data has no register. Named in the sources are two field IDs masked on the case record view, an identity number, a phone number and a date of birth with their masked forms, and one masking version label, MASK-SIT-01, with no list of the fields it covers. No source states which of the 1,366 dictionary fields are personal, which roles may see which field clear, or what a masking version contains beyond its label. The default rule that an unlisted field is masked is stated once, in an exception acceptance criterion, and is adopted by the PRD as a rule; the field register stays a gap.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-005-05 'no masking rule in MASK-SIT-01 covers v_ace_customer.date_of_birth for any role ... the date of birth shows masked as XXXX-XX-XX'; AC-ALT-P4-005-01 'XXXXXXXXX1234' and 'XXXXXX5678'; AC-P4-007-01 'DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked masked'; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule with field_id varchar(16), unmasked boolean and masking_version, and no seed; NFR-039 and NFR-040 set the behaviour and no register; DL26 holds the masking rules for each role as open.
proposed: Produce the personal field register with its field IDs and its masked form per data type, the per-role unmasked list and a masking version label that names the register it belongs to, as the seed of the masking policy, and answer DL26 for it, so FR-P4-016 and FR-P4-017 are testable beyond the five fields the FSD names.

title: REQ-ACA-006 still requires an access entry for every read of the data lake copy, which Architecture v5 removes
source: Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.4 REQ-ACA-006; Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 section 4; Architecture v5 slide 37 (no data lake) and the DP-17 pattern in the Template and Rules R5.5 ('Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'); Decision Log v10 D-RCV-35 and D-RCV-36; Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-042
description: The requirement word for word asks for an access entry on every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy. The data lake is removed by Architecture v5 and by DP-17, and the reporting read model is built from events into rwb-reporting, so the third object no longer exists and the requirement as written cannot be met or tested. The PRD reads the third object as the data products, which is what a reader now reads, and records the wording change; the business requirement itself has not been re-issued.
evidence: BRD Program v4 'REQ-ACA-006 | Every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is written to the access log.'; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 'Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data'; Architecture v5 slide 37 removes the lake; NFR-042 repeats the same three objects.
area: rwb-access access log scope of the logged read
proposed: Re-issue REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 in the next business requirement version as 'every read of the case store, the document store and a data product', so the requirement, the functional specification and this PRD use one list of objects; nothing else in the requirement changes.

title: The case record view and its history timeline are listed as P4 features while the screen and its endpoints belong to rwb-case
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A1.2 FEAT-ACA-11 and FEAT-ACA-12, A2.11 and A2.12; FSD P4 A2.11 acceptance criteria points to RWB-E1-023; Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-case: GET /cases/{id}, /cases?queue=; case record) and slide 41 (P3 owns the case); plan split_plan.json (RWB-P3-E1023-APP 'Case record view v1, read only')
description: Two of the thirty P4 features are screens that rwb-access does not own. The case record view and its history timeline are the case service's screen and endpoints, the plan places the case record view under P3, and Architecture v5 gives rwb-case the case, its CMMN state and the case endpoints. The PRD therefore excludes both features from P4 scope and keeps only the part rwb-access supplies to them: the authorise answer, the scope filter and the masked rendering. The P4 acceptance set cannot include the screen, so the two features need a stated home and a traceable owner in the FSD.
evidence: FSD P4 A1.2 'FEAT-ACA-11 | Show the case record view read only | User | Gives one screen holding the case, its accounts, parties, collateral, documents and history'; A2.11 and A2.12 describe the screen; A2.11's acceptance table points to RWB-E1-023; split_plan.json carries RWB-P3-E1023-APP and RWB-P3-E1023-CON for that key; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P3 the case, its CMMN state and the case endpoint.
owner_role: Business analyst with the P3 product owner
proposed: Move FEAT-ACA-11 and FEAT-ACA-12 with their acceptance criteria to FSD P3 in the next version, and leave in FSD P4 only the authorise, scope and masking behaviour the screen consumes, so each feature has one owner and one acceptance set.

title: FEAT-ACA-15, the release checklist and go-live readiness, is a delivery activity inside the product feature list and has no product requirement
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A1.2 FEAT-ACA-15 and A2.15; BRD Program v4 section 5.4 (no requirement for it); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (no component, table or endpoint for it)
description: One of the thirty P4 features describes working a release checklist for tests, training, run books and rollback. It has no business requirement in the program document, no table, endpoint or component in the technical specification and no acceptance criterion that a product can be held to; it duplicates the delivery material of the programme. This PRD excludes it from the product scope and records that exclusion, so that the P4 feature count and the requirement count can be reconciled and no reader expects a build item.
evidence: FSD P4 A1.2 'FEAT-ACA-15 | Run the release checklist, training and go-live readiness | Admin | Works the checklist that says the release can go to production: tests, training, run books, rollback. | E1 | A2.15'; BRD Program v4 section 5.4 lists thirteen requirements and none covers a release checklist; TSD P4 T2 lists seven components and none covers it.
proposed: Retire FEAT-ACA-15 from the module feature list and carry the release checklist in the programme delivery plan, so the P4 feature list holds only behaviour that a product can be accepted against.

title: No performance target covers the authorise answer, although every request passes one, and the nearest targets belong to other objects
source: Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-008 (screen under 2 seconds), NFR-011 (rule evaluation under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile) and section 5 (targets still to set, DL11); Architecture v5 slide 14 ('REST Access: authorise (cached)'); FSD P4 A2.4 and A2.5
description: The authorise answer sits in front of every request of every service and has no target of its own. The only numbers available are a screen target and a rule-evaluation target, neither of which is the authorise answer, and the non-functional targets that remain unset are held under DL11. The PRD therefore states the requirement as a constraint on the screen budget and records that no separate target exists, rather than choosing a number; a load test at the busiest hour cannot assert a pass or a fail until the target is set.
evidence: NFR-008 'A screen responds within its target under normal load. Under 2 seconds'; NFR-011 'A rule evaluation at a routing decision completes inside the user's wait. Under 300 milliseconds per rule evaluation at the 95th percentile'; Non-Functional Specification section 5 and the DL11 status on NFR-007, NFR-011, NFR-020 and NFR-021; Architecture v5 slide 14 names the authorise answer as cached and gives no time.
proposed: Set one target for the authorise answer at the busiest hour, with the cache hit and the miss stated separately, and record it under DL11 beside the screen and rule-evaluation targets, so NFR-P4-001 becomes a testable number.
